**DE Fundamentals Assignment**

**Identifying Beejan Technologies Problems.**

1. Every company runs 2 systems; Operational and Analytical. Beejan Analytical strategy is clearly not in good shape.  
2. Delayed Reporting required to drive stakeholder decisions.  
3. Customer Service is now being impacted.

Beejan Tech. has to be subjected to a full data engineering life cycle to improve customer service and make data readily available for further insights needed to drive growth.

![][image1]

**Collection**  
![][image2]  
**Social Media**: Largely unstructured data since we expect posts or tweets from customers.

**Call center Logs**: This can be **structured** and **unstructured** depending on the data being collected.We will assume data being collected is **structured** (e.g agent\_id, call\_id,call\_duration, call\_outcome) and **unstructured** data. (e.g call recordings)

**Sms**: This is unstructured data.

**Website Form:** This is structured data

**Ingestion.**  
The business requirement is primarily reporting and analytics to make informed decisions. **Batch processing** is the required approach for moving from source to destination. All data sources will be subjected to batch processing. Looking at the volume of data being generated, **Incremental load** is also the way to go. For the data sources;

* Social Media: assume api ingestion from source (API)  
* Call center logs: assume file uploads for both call details and call audio (audio/CSV)  
* SMS: assume api ingestion from source (API)  
* Website form: assume csv files upload from source (CSV)

**Storage**  
We are clearly building an OLAP system that allows for analysis and decision making. Data lake is the preferred storage option because it can store both structured and unstructured data. We will also be using the Extract \-Load \- Transform strategy. We want to preserve the raw data and then transform later as analytical requirements can change from time to time, ELT gives that flexibility since it allows schema on read.  
**Transformation**.  
This is where cleaning the data comes in. Remember we still get our raw data from the load, For the cleaning, remove duplicates, standardize format, e.g phone number, datetime, channel, Trim whitespaces, separate invalid entries.   
For categorizing complaints, I will use keywords to group different categories. Complaints can be grouped into Network issues, billing issues etc.  
After transforming, my raw data is now in another transformed table ready for use.

**Serving**  
Beejan's major problem is the slow rate of report gathering. Now the transformed data can be served for users intending to use. Data analysts can connect via a visualisation tool (power bi, tableau etc) to the transformed and aggregated data. End users can easily get data from these analyst dashboards.

**Orchestration and Monitoring**  
For the pipeline run time, this will largely depend on the management SLA for reporting. Assuming there will be a dashboard providing insight into customer complaints, then maybe an hourly run rate for the pipeline will be required so that data is ready to serve. If the reports are due monthly, then a daily end of data should suffice.

To detect failures, I would set alerts to notify of pipeline failures so they are fixed immediately.

**DataOps**  
Expectation is that the entire pipeline would run in a virtual machine. Most likely a linux environment. My entire code for the pipeline build would have to be moved from my development area to prod. This is where we deploy the code to prod
